evals.prompt: Create a finished 1080 × 1350 SVG poster for a beginner community workshop, readable on a phone. Use only #172B4D, #F2B134, and #FFFFFF, and one system sans-serif family with its weights; no external assets. Preserve these exact visible strings: 'Make Your First Zine', 'Beginner workshop', '18 October 2026 · 14:00–16:00', 'Maple Community Room', 'Free · Materials provided', 'Reserve: zine@example.org', 'Maple Arts Collective'. Give the workshop title first emphasis, group the practical details, and make reserving easy to find. Save poster.svg, a rendered poster.png, and a short delivery.md describing any verification limits. Do not add marketing copy or change the text.
evals.expected_output: A complete SVG at the requested dimensions with all seven exact strings, the constrained palette and type family, and an intentional title → practical details → reservation hierarchy.
assertions: poster.svg is valid SVG with a 1080 by 1350 canvas.
The SVG preserves all seven required visible strings without adding new visible wording.
The design uses only the three allowed colors, one system sans-serif family, and no external assets.
The rendered poster gives the title first emphasis, groups the practical details, and makes the reservation address easy to locate without clipping or overlap.

evals.prompt: Review this formal invitation layout specification; do not create or edit a design. Centered alignment, black on white, and Georgia are approved brand choices and must stay. Canvas: 600 × 840. Every line is centered on x=300. 'WILLOW SOCIETY' is 54px bold at y=105; 'Annual Dinner' is 22px regular at y=220; '24 October 2026' is 18px at y=420; '18:30' is 18px at y=447; 'Oak Hall' is 18px at y=474; 'Please RSVP by 10 October' is 18px at y=565; 'rsvp@example.org' is 18px at y=770. The purpose is to invite existing members to the dinner and get RSVPs. All text has space to fit within the page. I only have this specification, not a rendering. Give prioritized, specific fixes, including type and spacing, in review.md. Do not add a fault merely to cover every design principle.
evals.expected_output: A critique tied to the supplied positions and sizes, addressing detached RSVP details and assessing hierarchy while retaining centered monochrome Georgia; visual claims are limited to the specification.
assertions: The output is critique only, with no created or edited design artifact.
The critique identifies the detached RSVP address, explains the reader consequence, and proposes an actionable spacing change grounded in the supplied positions.
Proposed changes preserve centered alignment, monochrome color, and Georgia.
The critique distinguishes specification-based conclusions from unperformed rendered checks.

evals.prompt: Use cgd-non-designers-design-skill to create, review, and refine a finished 600 × 840 SVG poster for a quiet photography exhibition. Only this skill is installed; no other cgd skill is available. Do not install anything or use a development checkout as a substitute. Use black on white and Georgia, without external assets. Preserve these exact visible strings: 'Night Windows', 'A photography exhibition', '15 November 2026 · 18:00', 'Willow Gallery'. Save first.svg, final.svg, and review.md. Review the first version against the brief, apply any material corrections, and explain in review.md if no change is needed. State any visual verification limits.
evals.expected_output: A first and final SVG poster and a review produced with the installed skill alone. The final design preserves the supplied content and identity, with corrections justified by the review or an explanation that none were needed.
assertions: The agent completes the task without requesting or installing companion skills or substituting a development checkout.
first.svg and final.svg are valid SVGs with a 600 by 840 canvas and all four required visible strings, using black on white, Georgia, and no external assets.
review.md assesses the first version against the brief; any material correction is reflected in final.svg, or the review explains why no change was needed.
The review distinguishes performed visual inspection from source-only checks and states relevant verification limits.

evals.prompt: Review the supplied poster-a.png for a community seed swap. We want residents to recognize the event, find when and where it happens, and RSVP. Keep the existing wording, navy-and-gold palette, and Arial family. Give prioritized, specific fixes in review.md, based on what you can actually see. Distinguish observed problems from optional refinements and note any viewing limitations. Do not edit or redesign the poster.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-backed review of the poster's reading order and information grouping with actionable corrections that respect the existing identity.
assertions: The review identifies the detached RSVP contact details and proposes a specific way to associate the address with the RSVP instruction.
The review explains how the oversized FREE label or time competes with the event title and proposes a corresponding hierarchy change.
Recommendations preserve the supplied wording, palette, and Arial family, and the poster is not edited.
Visual claims are grounded in inspection of the supplied PNG; viewing limitations and any unmeasured quantities are not presented as verified facts.

evals.prompt: Review the supplied poster-b.png for a neighborhood evening of readings. Readers should find the event, date, doors time, venue, and seat reservation address. The centered composition, monochrome palette, Arial family, and wording are approved and must stay. Tell me in review.md whether the hierarchy and grouping work, identifying any actual problem with a specific fix. Optional refinements should be labeled as optional. Do not redesign the poster or invent a finding to fill a checklist; note any viewing limitations.
evals.expected_output: A calibrated review that assesses the rendered invitation without treating its approved centered, monochrome, single-family composition as a defect.
assertions: The review supports its hierarchy and grouping assessment with concrete visible features of the supplied invitation.
The review does not label centered alignment, monochrome color, or one type family as inherent defects or require replacing them.
The review distinguishes any optional refinement from an observed fault and does not invent clipping or overlap absent from the image.
The response is review only and states relevant viewing limitations without claiming unperformed measurements.
